issues.display_title: Issue #841: Room And Area Object Redefinition
issues.main_description_html:
Design and frontend integration for Room And Area Object Redefinition, per:

  • PRD: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-28-room-area-object-redefinition/prd.md
  • Brief: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-28-room-area-object-redefinition/brief.md

RESULT

Branch: design/room-and-area-object-redefinition

MapThru currently treats automatically detected wall-enclosed spaces and manually drawn polygon spaces as one shared object family. A wall-generated space sits next to a hand-drawn polygon in the same list, inherits the same controls, and implies the same lifecycle — so it is unclear what can be reshaped, deleted, typed, heightened, linked, or converted.

This task splits the taxonomy into two objects: Room is detected automatically inside a closed wall loop, Area is a manually drawn standalone closed polygon. This PRD supersedes docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-19-closed-room-type/prd.md, where both were still one object family; Closed Room color, logo, and object-protection behavior stays valid and now applies only to Rooms whose type is Closed.

Scope

  • Room lifecycle — a Room appears automatically when walls form a closed loop and takes its polygon from that loop. It cannot stand alone, cannot be manually reshaped, cannot be manually deleted (list, selection controls, keyboard Delete, context actions), and cannot be converted to Area. Breaking the loop by any wall delete/move/split/merge/edit removes the Room from the floor.
  • Room configuration — name and rename, one Information link, Event eligibility only after Information exists, Room height control, and Room type: Room, Hallway, Open (existing open-to-below behavior), Closed (existing Closed Room color, logo, incompatible-object cleanup, and placement blocking).
  • Room List — a list containing only wall-detected Rooms, with a Room icon distinct from the Area icon, the Room name as row title, and the Room type as row subtitle. No delete icon and no Convert To Area.
  • Area lifecycle — created with the custom Area polygon tool and only when the polygon is closed with at least three vertices. Stands alone without walls, can be moved, reshaped by vertex editing (drag to move; add/remove where the editor's existing geometry pattern allows), and deleted from selection controls, keyboard Delete, or the Area List delete icon.
  • Area configuration — name and rename, one Information link, Event eligibility only after Information exists. Flat in this release: no Room height control, no Room type values, no Closed Room color/logo/protection.
  • Area List — a list containing only standalone Areas, with the Area icon, the Area name as row title, no type subtitle, and a delete icon for editors.
  • Area selection controls — Area selected state, Delete Area, Convert To Room, Clear selection. No Room height, Room type, Closed color, or Closed logo controls. Only the single-selected-Area case is required here.
  • Convert To Room — validates the polygon has at least three vertices, generates one straight wall per polygon edge including the closing edge back to the first vertex, removes the standalone Area, and lets room detection create the Room from the resulting closed loop. The new Room keeps the Area's name and Information link and becomes selected when practical. Full boundary generation only — reusing or avoiding overlapping walls is out of scope. Invalid or self-intersecting polygons fail calmly and leave the Area unchanged; if no Room is detected the conversion must not leave the user with a deleted Area and no Room. Reversible through existing undo where editor history supports it.
  • Linked records — deleting an Area, or breaking a Room's wall loop, removes only the map object link. Information and Event records are never deleted automatically, and recreating a similar loop does not relink them.
  • Migration — standalone Areas previously saved with a Closed type are interpreted as flat Areas without Closed-only controls.

Out of scope

Backend REST API changes (unless persistence genuinely cannot distinguish Room from Area without a minimal field); billing, publishing, sharing, account, role, or permission changes; search matching; route calculation; Event model expansion; Room-to-Area conversion; manual Room vertex editing; curved walls from Convert To Room; Area height or Area type controls; persisting a broken Room as a standalone object; replacing existing wall, door, window, shape, point, access, or safety tools.

Acceptance

  • Closing walls creates a Room automatically; deleting or opening one enclosing wall removes it.
  • Room shape changes only by editing walls — no manual reshape, no manual delete, no Convert To Area.
  • Room can be renamed, linked to Information, and linked to Event only after Information exists.
  • Room height control remains, and Room type choices are Room, Hallway, Open, and Closed.
  • Closed Room color, logo, incompatible-object cleanup, and placement blocking still work and appear only for Closed Rooms.
  • Room List shows only Rooms, with a distinct icon, name as title, type as subtitle, and no delete action.
  • Area can be created only as a closed polygon, stands alone without walls, and can be selected, moved, vertex-edited, renamed, and deleted.
  • Area can be linked to Information, and to Event only after Information exists.
  • Area shows no height control, no Room type control, and no Closed Room color or logo controls.
  • Area List shows only standalone Areas and includes a delete icon for editors.
  • Area selection controls include Delete Area and Convert To Room.
  • Convert To Room generates straight walls around every Area polygon edge, removes the Area, creates a detected Room, and preserves the Area name and Information link.
  • Convert To Room can be undone where existing editor history supports it.
  • Breaking a Room does not delete Information or Event records.
  • Search, route, publishing, billing, account, and permission behavior remain unchanged.
